text:
Jackson Blake was a fourth-round pick in 2021. Now he's a Stanley Cup champion and one of the reasons Carolina keeps winning. He's playing 17 minutes and 43 seconds a night, he's on the ice for 82% of the Hurricanes' power-play chances (40% last season), and he has 24 points in 25 games, including the winner at the Rangers on Nov. 22.

The underlying numbers are startling. With Blake on the ice at five on five, Carolina gets 67% of the expected goals, and Cory Lavalette of the North State Journal noted he's been below 50% of shot attempts just three times all season. Dimitri Filipovic of The Hockey PDOcast called him "an absolute dog this season."

Two things are pulling in opposite directions. His own finishing is behind (eight goals on 10.8 expected), while his team has scored 5.9 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. One should rise, the other should fade. Evolving-Hockey also notes he plays with strong teammates. Our range has him at 57 to 78 points, a big step from 0.65 a game last season.
